newsitem.title: USA: Apache sets Australian natgas sales.
newsitem.headline: Apache sets Australian natgas sales.

text.p: Apache Corp said Tuesday Boral Ltd has tentatively agreed to purchase about 40 billion cubic feet of natural gas from the Harriet Joint Venture in Western Australia over a 10-year period.
Daily volumes of some 12 million cubic feet are expected to come from the Wonnich gas field, with initial deliveries slated for April 1998, Apache said.
Apache operates the Harriet Joint Venture, holding a 22.5 percent interest.

Remaining participants are: Ampolex Ltd with 25 percent; Kufpec Australia Pty Ltd with 19.3 percent; Novus Petroleum Ltd with 12.5 percent; TAP (Harriet) Pty Ltd with 12.2 percent; and Hardy Oil & Gas Plc with 8.4 percent.

The Wonnich natural gas field is located offshore Western Australia about 20 miles from the Apache-operated Harriet Joint Venture production facilities on Varanus Island, the company said. Natural gas will be treated at that plant and delivered through to the Goldfields Gas Transmission and Dampier-to-Bunbury pipelines.

Boral will resell the natural gas through its Major Industry and Power Division to customers along the Goldfields Gas Transmission pipeline and in southwestern Western Australia. The contract is subject to various conditions including government approval for development of Wonnich field, Apache said.

"The most significant aspect of securing a gas sales contract is that it makes it economically viable for us to proceed with the installation of production facilities at Wonnich field," the company said.
"While this contract will enable us to book only a small portion of the estimated reserves from Wonnich, we'll continue to pursue additional sales agreements for the balance of the field's reserves."
This sales agreement brings Apache's total net natural gas reserves under contract in Western Australia to some 75 billion cubic feet, it said.
